**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/26 (Fri) 07:16  
[EVENT] User is planning to make chicken fajitas again this weekend.  
[PREFERENCE] User wants to make sure the marinade for the chicken is just right.  
[FACT] User mentioned that the marinade for the chicken fajitas included olive oil, which added to the flavor.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Marinating chicken can enhance flavor and tenderness; tips include using acidic ingredients, oil, balancing flavors, and marinating times.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended a marinade for chicken fajitas: 1/2 cup olive oil, 1/4 cup lime juice, 2 cloves garlic (minced), 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin, salt and pepper to taste.  
[PREFERENCE] User is thinking of adding bell peppers to the marinade.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Bell peppers can add flavor and texture; marinating them can enhance their taste but should be limited to 30 minutes to 1 hour to avoid mushiness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested using a gentle marinade for bell peppers and adjusting cooking time since they may cook faster than chicken.  
[PREFERENCE] User is considering using fresh onions in the marinade.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fresh onions can be a good addition but may overpower other flavors; suggested sautéing onions and garlic before adding them to the marinade for better flavor and texture.  
[PREFERENCE] User plans to sauté the onions and garlic before adding them to the marinade.  
[EVENT] User is thinking of making guacamole to go with the fajitas.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided tips on choosing the right avocados for guacamole, including looking for ripeness, checking color, weight, and avoiding brown spots.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended using Hass or Fuerte avocados for their creamy texture.  
[PREFERENCE] User is thinking of adding fresh cilantro to the guacamole.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fresh cilantro is a great addition to guacamole, balancing flavors and adding freshness; suggested chopping it finely and adding it just before serving.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Mentioned that cilantro is a staple herb in Mexican cuisine, making it a natural fit for guacamole.
